To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
public opinion is volatile, context dependent and biased.
the public is not yet ready for autonomous driving.
public opinion of autonomous vehicles can be obtained in a user centred way, and that it is necessary to take account of a range of biases that can affect responses to questions on this topic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we can develop a user centred method for design of HMI concepts that can be used in the design and development of autonomous vehicles.
the development of a methodology for the design of HMI for autonomous vehicles.
developing a method for understanding public opinion on autonomous driving and the design of the human machine interface for autonomous vehicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the public is still in a state of flux with regard to autonomous vehicle technology, but is capable of expressing its views in a rational and coherent way, if given the right tools to do so.
the methodology described here is capable of addressing the issues raised above.
the public is very sensitive to the potential of the autonomous car, but that there are a number of key issues that can only be addressed in a user centred manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the public is very interested in autonomous vehicle technology, but that there is considerable uncertainty about how to design the user interface and the user experience.
the design of autonomous vehicles must be inclusive of the wider population and not just the 'average' user.
the public is not ready for autonomous vehicles and that a significant proportion of the population would not want to use them.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are a large number of issues that need to be addressed in the development of a user centric design capable method for autonomous vehicles that is inclusive and that addresses the wider population.

there is a need to develop a method that is able to address the issues of bias and context in public opinion surveys, and to provide the basis for a more inclusive approach to design for autonomous vehicle HMI.
there is a need for a method to capture public opinion on autonomous driving in an unbiased way, and to use this data to inform design of HMI for driverless vehicles.
